purpose: Initial bounded live calibration of evidence-first Fast against owner-reviewed, independent authoritative baselines.

sources.adjudication: Independent known-fact baselines below; Fast output is never its own ground truth.

cases.why: Clean large-cap control with comparable SEC financial history.
known_baseline: Quarterly revenue and net income increased on the prior-year comparison.
Nine-month operating cash flow increased and aligned free cash flow is positive.
Cash remains substantial while commercial paper and notes declined.
Bounded absence of a risk must not be represented as proof that no risk exists.

cases.why: Compound capital-structure case with issuance, exchangeable notes, debt, liquidity pressure, and a completed reverse split.
known_baseline: Revenue improved on quarterly and six-month comparisons.
Quarterly loss worsened while the six-month loss improved; the periods must remain distinct.
Six-month operating cash flow turned positive and aligned simple free cash flow is positive.
Recent issuance and note exchanges materially increased shares outstanding.
The issuer completed a 1-for-10 reverse split and retains material future financing and dilution risk.

cases.why: Small-cap reporting-conflict, going-concern, convertible-financing, and active-listing-pressure case.
known_baseline: Revenue declined and shares outstanding increased materially.
Annual evidence disclosed losses, negative operating cash flow, negative working capital, and going-concern uncertainty.
Nasdaq minimum-bid compliance remains unresolved.
Recent non-reliance evidence makes affected historical financial values conflicting; they must not produce favorable scores.
Convertible-note activity supports material future-dilution risk.

cases.why: Small-cap distress case with active listing deficiencies, losses, warrants, and prospective reverse-split authority.
known_baseline: Cash is low, losses continue, operating cash flow is negative, and accumulated deficit is material.
Revenue and operating cash flow deteriorated on available comparisons.
Material weaknesses and Nasdaq bid-price and stockholders-equity deficiencies are active risks.
Reverse-split authorization supports prospective risk but is not a completed historical split.
Warrants and increasing shares support capital-structure risk.

cases.why: Strong operating-trend case with material accounting-control warnings and newer preliminary evidence.
known_baseline: Comparable revenue and net income grew strongly.
Material weaknesses in internal control remain a serious accounting warning.
Newer preliminary results may inform catalyst and current context but must not silently replace standardized periodic trend data.
Strong operating trends must not erase the accounting warning.

relative_ordering: AMC, NCPL, and NXL must show materially greater confirmed capital-risk evidence than AAPL and SMCI.
NXL and NCPL must show materially greater listing/reverse-split pressure than AAPL and SMCI.
SMCI and AAPL should have the strongest supported revenue trends; AMC should improve; NCPL and NXL should be weaker or unresolved.
AAPL should have the strongest financial resilience; NCPL and NXL should be weakest or unresolved; SMCI operating strength must not hide its accounting warning.
completion_rule: Issue #55 remains open if any critical category is sparsely sampled or any severe misleading miss is unresolved.
